1.text: | **I01** | `O_candidate(s,d,W)` depends only on inherited LRS3 candidacy and legitimate entry of `W`; no SH/regime/Gate2/path/final result may affect membership. | Integrity failure |

2.text: | **I02** | Every candidate `T` must resolve exactly one strict-C10 predecessor `G(T)` satisfying `G<T`; exact-grid observations consume the preceding endpoint. | Integrity failure |

3.text: | **I03** | `G_candidate` is the deduplicated set of candidate strict-C10 endpoints. | Integrity failure |

4.text: | **I04** | `SH(s,d,W)` exists **iff** `|O_candidate|>0`; empty candidate set ⇒ SH undefined, never ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE. | Integrity failure |

5.text: | **I05** | For nonempty candidates, aggregate SH is ELIGIBLE **iff every unique candidate endpoint** passes W-specific endpoint SH authorization. | Integrity failure |

6.text: | **I06** | A candidate-bearing day contributes **all or none** of its candidates to D1 according to aggregate SH. No partial day inclusion. | Integrity failure |

7.text: | **I07** | D1 contains observations only and cannot be filtered by D3, regime state, Gate2, `SH_path`, or final disposition. | Integrity failure |

8.text: | **I08** | `D1=∅` ⇒ D0 terminal `NO_TARGET_OBSERVATION_POPULATION`; C1 vs C2 provenance remains distinguishable. No fallback or synthetic Gate2 result. | `D0_TERMINAL` |

9.text: | **I09** | `D1≠∅` ⇒ D0 passes. No additional minimum-observation threshold may be introduced. | Integrity failure if violated |

10.text: | **I10** | D2 may be constructed only after D0 passes and must equal the complete 5-minute grid from `G(T_first)` through `G(T_last)`, inclusive. | Integrity failure |

11.text: | **I11** | D2 boundaries derive **only** from D1 extrema; excluded candidates cannot establish or extend them. | Integrity failure |

12.text: | **I12** | Once constructed, D2 is immutable. Interior exclusions or D3 failures never create holes, shrink, expand, or re-anchor it. | Integrity failure |

13.text: | **I13** | A one-cell D2 where `G_first=G_last` is valid and must not be rejected merely for its size. | Integrity failure |

14.text: | **I14** | Exactly one authoritative `D3_ADMISSIBLE(G,W)` exists for **every** endpoint in D2. | Integrity failure |

15.text: | **I15** | D3 must satisfy `SH_AUTHORIZED(G,W) AND REGIME_STATE_VALID(G,W)` with SH authorization evaluated first. | Integrity failure |

16.text: | **I16** | `SH_AUTHORIZED=FALSE` forces D3 FALSE regardless of mechanically available HIGH/LOW state; mechanically computed unauthorized state has no classification authority. | Integrity failure |

17.text: | **I17** | D3 FALSE leaves the cell in D2 but prevents environmental classification/episode continuity; failure provenance remains auditable. | Integrity failure |

18.text: | **I18** | For every `T∈D1`, current-W regime eligibility equals authoritative D3 at strict-C10 `G(T)` and cannot mutate D1 or D2. | Integrity failure |

19.text: | **I19** | D4 is produced by one chronological sweep over the **complete D3 timeline**, not observation-filtered D1 endpoints. | Integrity failure |

20.text: | **I20** | Every episode is a maximal contiguous same-state run of D3-admissible cells. Exactly three boundary causes exist: `STATE_CHANGE`, `D3_INADMISSIBILITY`, `D2_BOUNDARY`. | Integrity failure |

21.text: | **I21** | D3-inadmissible cells terminate continuity, form no episode, create no censoring, and cannot be bridged. | Integrity failure |

22.text: | **I22** | Only literal D2 boundaries may censor. Pre-D2 left tracing uses inherited state-transition / inherited-validity-discontinuity authority without extending D2. | Integrity failure |

23.text: | **I23** | Every episode reaching `G_last` is right-censored; post-D2 evidence cannot remove/rescue that flag. | Integrity failure |

24.text: | **I24** | Left/right censoring are independent; a one-cell episode may carry either/both/neither and has observed duration exactly 5 minutes. | Integrity failure |

25.text: | **I25** | `K_HIGH`, `K_LOW`, `K_total`, and `T_classified` derive exclusively from authoritative D3/D4 environmental topology. | Integrity failure |

30.text: | **I30** | `R_W`, `A_W`, and `H_W` remain distinct: `R_W` complete reasons, `A_W` sole routing authority, `H_W` diagnostic only. | Integrity failure |

45.text: | **I45** | Integrity failure at any layer cannot be translated into `R_W`, `A_W`, `H_W`, D0, source-history exclusion, regime ineligibility, or another ordinary methodological result. | Fail closed |

46.text: | **I46** | Partial ordinary results existing before integrity failure may remain as audit evidence but acquire **no downstream authorization authority**. | Fail closed |

48.text:
> **I48 — D4 upstream immutability.**  
> `D4_W(s)` may partition and summarize the fixed `D2_W(s)` domain but must not resize or rebuild D2, alter any authoritative D3 value, or rebuild D3.  
> **Violation → methodology-integrity failure.**

50.text:
> **I50 — Eligibility-layer naming discipline.**  
> Whenever more than one eligibility layer is in scope, an implementation artifact, schema, diagnostic, or interface must identify the applicable eligibility layer explicitly rather than use an unqualified `eligibility` field/status whose authority is ambiguous. Inherited LRS3 eligibility, source-history eligibility, current-Window regime eligibility, and final observation eligibility must remain semantically distinguishable.  
> **Violation → interface/schema non-compliance. Verified through static interface-conformance review; it is not itself a runtime discriminated `INTEGRITY_FAILURE` result.**

51.text:
> **I51 — Authoritative-object non-substitutability.**  
> A methodological consumer must consume the authoritative object required by its interface. Predictable implication, numerical equality, compatible Boolean value, shared provenance, or reconstructibility does not authorize substitution by a different methodological object, including an object with different index arity, semantic type, dependency stage, or producer.  
> **Violation → methodology-integrity failure.**

52.text:
> **I52 — Single authoritative producer.**  
> Within its applicable Window Evaluation or final-path projection, each authoritative methodological object must have exactly one authoritative producer. Derived evidence may validate, reconcile, or report that object but must not become a competing authoritative producer.  
> **Violation → methodology-integrity failure.**

53.text:
> **I53 — Control/provenance type preservation.**  
> `D0Termination`, `DiagnosticRecord`, `R_W`, `A_W`, `H_W`, `ApplicabilityStatus`, `BoundaryCause`, `CensoringStatus`, and `Episode` are distinct authority-bearing control/provenance object types and must not be coerced into or substituted for one another. Their respective provenance and semantic roles must remain explicit.  
> **Violation → methodology-integrity failure.**
